processes.description: Desk leads and managers arrange classes, system sessions and presentations for their staff. A round starts when a lead proposes a session or a course comes up: they pick topics, choose who attends, sometimes build balanced class rosters, and ask the training side to sign people up. Staff also ask whether they may enrol in a suggested course, and a supervisor approves the registration. Timing is fitted around shifts and other commitments, and session details, timelines and changes are circulated to the group.
steps: A lead or manager proposes a class, presentation or system session and its topics.
The lead picks attendees, sometimes building class rosters of equal strength.
Attendees are signed up, or staff ask whether they may enrol in a suggested course.
A supervisor approves the course registration in the training system.
Timing is arranged around shifts, such as asking night shift staff to come in early.
Session details, timelines and any changes are circulated to the group.

stalls.summary: Approving a course registration fails with an error in the system, so the approval cannot be completed as sent.
An organiser writes that news from the night before forces a change, reopening arrangements that had already been made.

automation.approach: A shared training tracker listing each session with its topic, date, attendees, shift and approval status, filled from a simple sign-up form. Leads choose attendees in the tracker, the training side registers from it, and approvals are checked off there instead of being assembled from separate messages.
automation.rationale: Most of a round is assembling lists of names, signing them up and tracking approvals and timing. A standard tracker layout keeps attendee lists, rosters and approval status in a single place, while choosing topics and people stays with the leads.

work_estimate.rationale: Minutes go to choosing attendees and building rosters, registering named staff for a class or pilot, approving registrations and arranging shift timing. Most rounds name a few people and a class, so the work is modest; building balanced rosters for a class series sits at the high end. Registration lists and approval tracking suit a template; choosing people does not.

processes.description: The commercial and supply side tells logistics about changes to gas supply. A round starts with a notice or a forward: a new well coming on with its expected volume, a producer deal that has been continued, a plant processing election for the month, or where a producer's gas should flow. Logistics schedulers read it and adjust deals, nominations and flow paths to match, and the sender sometimes has to chase the producer for confirmation.
steps: Supply or commercial staff learn of a change: a new well, a continued deal, a processing election or a new flow path.
They send or forward a notice to logistics with the producer, volumes and timing.
Schedulers update the deal, nomination or delivery point to match.
Where the producer must confirm, the sender follows up by phone and email.
Logistics leads forward the notice to the schedulers who handle the affected points.

stalls.summary: A requested change of flow waits on the producer, who has not answered repeated voice and email contacts.

automation.approach: A standard supply change notice with fixed fields: producer, well or meter, effective date and time, expected volume, processing election and delivery point. Logistics can then update deals and nominations straight from the notice, and an open item stays flagged until the producer confirms.
automation.rationale: The notices are short free-text messages carrying the same handful of facts each time. A fixed template makes sure volume, timing and flow path arrive together, which cuts the lookup and follow-up schedulers do before entering the change.

work_estimate.rationale: Minutes go to entering the change in the deal and nomination records: continuing a deal, setting up a new well's volumes, applying the processing election or moving gas to a different line, plus checking it with the producer. Each notice covers a single change, so the work is short; an unresponsive producer pushes it toward the high end. Entry from a structured notice can be partly automated; confirming with producers cannot.

processes.description: Desk staff report problems with trading, scheduling and position tools and ask for enhancements. A round starts with an error, a wrong position or flow figure, missing curve data or a feed that is down, or with a customer or desk need for a new feature. IT answers with a cause, a workaround or a fix; enhancement lists are compiled and reviewed in requirements and use-case sessions; desks name testers for rebuilt or new releases; and IT announces outages, migrations and maintenance windows that desks must confirm or plan around.
steps: A user hits an error, a wrong figure or missing data in a tool, or sees a need for a new feature.
The user reports it to IT or the application team, often copying the desk lead.
IT replies with a cause or workaround, such as an unmapped drive, or schedules a fix.
Enhancement requests are compiled into lists and discussed in requirements or use-case sessions.
Desks name testers who test rebuilt or new releases before they go live.
IT announces outages, migrations and maintenance windows and asks desks to confirm timing.
Desk leads forward fixes, new features and notices to their groups.

stalls.summary: Tools fail during daily work: errors launching a program, approving or importing finals, server errors at login and a data scrape down through a night shift.
Position and flow tools show wrong or incomplete figures, such as a short position, excessive flow or a missing curve, which staff must catch and chase.
Planned outages and maintenance take scheduling and trading systems offline, and IT has to ask desks when a shutdown can happen.
Enhancements linger: a position manager rework demonstrated months earlier is raised again, and a manager complains of a lack of accountability and urgency.
Local setup problems, such as installing a tool on a desktop or an unmapped drive, cause errors that need IT help.
Requirements and test sessions are rescheduled to fit around other meetings.

contradictions.summary: The testing request asks each desk for a single designated tester, while a desk answers that two people will share the role.

automation.approach: A single issue and enhancement intake form (system, symptom, steps to reproduce, desk, impact) feeding a tracked list with owner and status, a published outage and maintenance calendar that desks confirm against, and a known-fixes checklist for common local errors such as drive mapping and browser paths.
automation.rationale: Problems arrive as free-text emails and forwards, and enhancement lists are compiled by hand. A standard intake form gives IT what it needs to reproduce an issue the first time and lets owners and status be tracked, which addresses the lingering items and accountability complaints; diagnosing and testing stay with people.

work_estimate.rationale: Minutes go to reproducing and documenting a failure, checking a wrong position or flow against other data, compiling enhancement lists and testing rebuilt releases. A simple outage notice needs little work, while a position discrepancy or a test phase takes much longer, hence the wide range. Intake, status tracking and outage notices suit a template; diagnosis and testing do not.
